top_choice_rationale: P002 (Helpman and Melitz) rewards a mature, general framework in which firm heterogeneity, selection into exporting and reallocation across firms drive the gains from trade. Its core predictions have been tested on firm-level and transaction-level data in many countries for over twenty years. That direct confrontation with micro data is the criterion I weight most. The attribution weaknesses are real: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are uncredited, Helpman's marginal credit must be separated from Krugman's 2008 prize, and the size of the welfare gains depends on functional form. A citation limited to selection and reallocation can manage these. P001 (Kiyotaki and Moore) is a close second. Its attribution is cleaner, and I now judge the 2022 overlap to be mainly a wording issue. But the collateral channel is established more as a modelling building block than as a directly measured magnitude. P003 is well scrutinised but weaker on separable attribution and on marginal credit after recent prizes. No award is ranked last because at least two proposals are serious, mature achievements.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my listed co-authors are not credited in P001, P002 or P003, and my Stockholm University overlap with IIES colleagues is institutional, not a tie to any candidate
